To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a single augmentation strategy may be used uniformly across tasks and datasets, (2) learned augmentation policies can be found without a separate search phase, (3) learned augmentation policies may be tuned to the dataset and model size, and (4) learned augmentation policies improve the robustness of deep models to common corruptions.

1) we propose an interpretable augmentation policy that may be trained with the model and dataset size of interest, 2) we demonstrate that this policy leads to state of the-art results on CIFAR 100 and ImageNet and 3) we demonstrate that the policy is effective across different tasks and models, including object detection

RandAugment: (a) achieves state of the art performance on CIFAR10, CIFAR100, SVHN and ImageNet, (b) achieves state of art performance on object detection, and (c) can be trained with no separate search phase and is able to adjust regularization strength based on dataset and model size.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, “Can we learn to augment images without a separate search phase?” We show that the answer is yes and that the resulting approach is simple, effective, and interpretable.

the following questions: How much data augmentation is too much? How much data augmentation do we need? How much does it help? How do different augmentation policies affect generalization? How does data augmentation affect robustness?

the question of whether learned augmentation strategies may be used in a black box manner, with no separate search phase, and whether learned augmentation strategies can be used to automatically adjust their strength.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RandAugment is the new state of the art in data augmentation for image classification and object recognition.
RandAugment is a practical augmentation strategy for training deep networks.
RandAugment can achieve the same performance as AutoAugment with less training time and no search phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a simple yet effective data augmentation method that can be applied to any model and dataset without the need for a separate search phase and can be used uniformly on different tasks.
we propose a simple yet powerful data augmentation strategy that can be applied to any model and any dataset with no need for separate search.
data augmentation is not a fixed recipe but a hyperparameter that can be adjusted based on model and dataset size and that learned augmentation is not an exception but the new norm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, interpretable data augmentation policy may be used uniformly across datasets and models and can achieve state of the art performance.
data augmentation can be made practical without sacrificing performance.
